```{r}
here::i_am("report/decisions.qmd")
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

universe <- read_rds(here("data", "processed", "universe.rds"))
pct <- function(x, d = 1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 10^-d)

# Possessions kept by every rule except the one a section is about
not_garbage_or_last2 <- universe %>% filter(!excl_last2min, !excl_garbage, !is.na(net_points))
analysed <- universe %>% filter(!excluded, !is.na(net_points))
```

Every definition in this project was a choice. This log records each one: the question, the
options, the evidence, and where the decision came from. **Basketball** marks decisions that came
from how the game is played; **Statistics** marks decisions driven by the data or the model. All
numbers below are computed from the data when this page is rendered (NBA regular seasons 2023-24
and 2024-25); see [Data notes](data-notes.qmd) for the validation of the raw sources.

# What counts as "pushing after a make"

## Only possessions after a made field goal, not after a made free throw

*Origin: rules.* After a made field goal the game clock keeps running during the inbound; after a
free throw it is stopped until the inbound is touched (NBA Rule 5). Time to the first action
would include the inbound in one case and not in the other, so only made field goals are used.

## Intention is a continuous pace, not a fast-break count

*Origin: Basketball, confirmed by the data.* The first definition was the FIBA fast-break rule
(first action within 8 s). It turned out to describe a fast break, not the decision to push: a
team that pushes after a make usually ends in early offense, around 8–12 s, and a push that the
defense stops looks like any long possession.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fastbreak
#| tbl-cap: "Share of possessions after a made field goal by time to first action"
analysed %>%
  group_by(Season = season) %>%
  summarise(
    `Δ ≤ 8 s (FIBA fast break)` = pct(mean(delta_s <= 8)),
    `Δ ≤ 12 s` = pct(mean(delta_s <= 12)),
    `Median Δ (s)` = median(delta_s)
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-team-range
#| tbl-cap: "Team-seasons differ by about 4 seconds in their average pace after makes"
analysed %>%
  group_by(season, team) %>%
  summarise(mean_delta = mean(delta_s), le12 = mean(delta_s <= 12), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Season = season) %>%
  summarise(
    Fastest = team[which.min(mean_delta)],
    `Fastest Δ (s)` = round(min(mean_delta), 1),
    Slowest = team[which.max(mean_delta)],
    `Slowest Δ (s)` = round(max(mean_delta), 1),
    `Range of share Δ ≤ 12 s` = paste(pct(min(le12), 0), "to", pct(max(le12), 0))
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

With only about 5% of possessions as strict fast breaks, a per-game fast-break rate would rest
on about two possessions. The average time to the first action uses every possession and
separates teams clearly. Decision: intention is the team-game average time to the first action,
with no cut-off fixed in advance.

## The inbound is part of pushing

*Origin: Basketball.* The moment the ball is touched in bounds is not in any public data, so the
inbound cannot be removed. It should not be: inbounding quickly is part of pushing. The part
every team takes is a constant that cancels out of the within-team comparison.

## Time to first action, not possession length

*Origin: Statistics.* Possession length is also available, but it grows with offensive rebounds
and ends at the defensive rebound after a miss, which is sometimes logged late. It is kept as a
robustness check.

# When the clock, not the team, sets the pace

## The last 54 seconds of quarters 1–3 are excluded

*Origin: Basketball, confirmed by the data.* Near the end of a quarter, teams shoot early to get
a 2-for-1, hold for the last shot, or heave. Time to the first action then reflects the clock,
not a choice to push.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-end-quarter
#| tbl-cap: "Quarters 1-3: possessions that start in the last 54 seconds against the rest"
not_garbage_or_last2 %>%
  filter(period <= 3) %>%
  mutate(Window = if_else(start_s <= 54, "Last 54 s of the quarter", "Rest of the quarter")) %>%
  group_by(Window) %>%
  summarise(
    Possessions = n(),
    `Mean Δ (s)` = round(mean(delta_s), 1),
    `Fast breaks (Δ ≤ 8 s)` = pct(mean(delta_s <= 8))
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

## The last 2:00 of the 4th quarter and of overtime are excluded

*Origin: rules.* The game clock stops after made baskets there, so the inbound is no longer
inside the time to the first action.

## Garbage time follows Cleaning the Glass, without the starters condition

*Origin: Statistics.* The margin thresholds of Cleaning the Glass are applied (4th quarter only:
25, 20 and 10 points by time left). Its second condition, two or fewer starters on the floor,
cannot be applied because the data have no lineups, so slightly more possessions are excluded.

# Separating the score from the choice to push

## Three analyses: full, close and first quarter

*Origin: Basketball.* Teams behind push to catch up and teams ahead slow down, so the score can
drive pace. The same model is fitted on all possessions, on close possessions, and on first
quarters only, where the game starts tied and the plan is not yet shaped by the score.

## The score moves the pace, inside every team

*Origin: Basketball, confirmed by the data.* The first fit of the main model, on all
possessions, gave a small negative return: in games where a team played faster than usual after
makes, those possessions went slightly worse. Teams that are behind speed up to catch up, so the
games that go badly are also the faster ones. That alone can produce a negative association.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pace-by-score
#| tbl-cap: "Mean seconds to first action by score margin when the possession starts"
analysed %>%
  mutate(`Margin at the start` = cut(
    start_margin, c(-Inf, -10, -5, -1, 0, 4, 9, Inf),
    labels = c("Down 10+", "Down 5-9", "Down 1-4", "Tied", "Up 1-4", "Up 5-9", "Up 10+")
  )) %>%
  group_by(`Margin at the start`) %>%
  summarise(Possessions = n(), `Mean Δ (s)` = round(mean(delta_s), 1)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-within-score
#| tbl-cap: "Within each team-season: games played faster than usual are games with a worse score"
within_tg <- analysed %>%
  group_by(season, game_id, team) %>%
  summarise(mean_delta = mean(delta_s), mean_margin = mean(start_margin), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(season, team) %>%
  mutate(faster_than_usual = mean(mean_delta) - mean_delta,
         margin_dev = mean_margin - mean(mean_margin)) %>%
  summarise(r = cor(faster_than_usual, margin_dev), .groups = "drop")
within_tg %>%
  summarise(
    `Team-seasons` = n(),
    `Median correlation` = round(median(r), 2),
    `Team-seasons with a negative correlation` = sum(r < 0)
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

The correlation cannot separate "behind, so faster" from "faster, it went wrong, so behind":
the margin at each possession already includes the earlier possessions. That is why the model
is also fitted on close possessions and on first quarters, where the score has had little time
to build up.

## "Close" means within 5 points, in quarters 1–3

*Origin: Basketball, confirmed by the data.* Close games are played slower near the end, long
before the last two minutes.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-close-segment
#| tbl-cap: "Possessions that start within 5 points, by segment of the game"
analysed %>%
  filter(abs(start_margin) <= 5) %>%
  mutate(Segment = case_when(
    period <= 3 ~ "Quarters 1-3",
    period == 4 & start_s > 360 ~ "4th quarter, 12:00-6:00",
    period == 4 ~ "4th quarter, 6:00-2:00",
    TRUE ~ "Overtime"
  )) %>%
  group_by(Segment) %>%
  summarise(
    Possessions = n(),
    `Mean Δ (s)` = round(mean(delta_s), 1),
    `Fast breaks (Δ ≤ 8 s)` = pct(mean(delta_s <= 8))
  ) %>%
  arrange(`Mean Δ (s)`) %>%
  kable()
```

Keeping the 4th quarter would make a game look slow partly because it was close at the end.
"Close" is measured at the start of each possession, never by the final result: selecting games
by how they ended would condition on the outcome.

# What a possession is worth

## Net points: the cost of how a possession ends

*Origin: Basketball and Statistics.* A turnover costs more than the points not scored: it hands
the opponent a better possession. Each possession is charged with the value of the opponent's
next possession, estimated within the same season.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-next-value
#| tbl-cap: "Points per possession, by how the possession started (all possessions of each season)"
read_rds(here("data", "processed", "next_possession_values.rds")) %>%
  mutate(`Opponent's possession starts after our...` = case_when(
    str_detect(start_type, "Make") & start_type != "Off FT Make" ~ "made field goal",
    start_type == "Off Steal" ~ "live-ball turnover (steal)",
    start_type == "Off Dead Ball" ~ "dead ball (incl. dead-ball turnover)",
    str_detect(start_type, "Miss|Block") & start_type != "Off FT Miss" ~ "missed shot",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )) %>%
  filter(!is.na(`Opponent's possession starts after our...`)) %>%
  group_by(`Opponent's possession starts after our...`, season) %>%
  summarise(value = round(mean(value), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = season, values_from = value) %>%
  kable()
```

A live-ball turnover hands the opponent about 0.2 points more than a made basket does. That is the
cost the net points charge.

# Measuring intention with error

## The game's average pace is a noisy measurement

*Origin: Statistics.* A team-game has about 30 possessions after a made basket, and time to the
first action varies a lot within a game. Its average is therefore measured with error.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reliability
#| tbl-cap: "How much of the game-to-game variation in pace is measurement noise"
tg <- analysed %>%
  group_by(season, game_id, team) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_delta = mean(delta_s), sd_delta = sd(delta_s), .groups = "drop")
tg %>%
  group_by(Season = season) %>%
  summarise(
    `Possessions per team-game` = round(mean(n), 1),
    `Within-game SD of Δ (s)` = round(mean(sd_delta, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `Standard error of a game's mean (s)` = round(mean(sd_delta / sqrt(n), na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    `SD of game means (s)` = round(sd(mean_delta), 2)
  ) %>%
  mutate(`Share of variance that is noise` =
           pct(`Standard error of a game's mean (s)`^2 / `SD of game means (s)`^2, 0)) %>%
  kable()
```

Using the observed average directly as a predictor would bias the estimated return towards
zero. Decision: the true pace of each game is a latent parameter, measured by the observed
average with this known error.

## Team-game likelihood

*Origin: Statistics.* Net points per 100 of a team-game are an average of about 30 possessions,
close to normal by the central limit theorem, with a spread that shrinks with the number of
possessions. A possession-level model is a planned extension.

# Seasons

## Every quantity is paired with its own season

*Origin: Basketball.* Rosters and coaches change between seasons and within them. The unit is
the team-season, and no number from one season is used to describe or adjust another.

## 2025-26 is descriptive only in this version

*Origin: data availability.* Possession-level data for 2025-26 are not in the public dump used
here. The season of Miami's change of pace after Jimmy Butler's departure is described with
team totals from pbpstats.com; adding it to the model needs a possession parser for the new
play-by-play format, planned as the first update.
